openings.claim: A slot-mounted cradle replaces magnetic dependence with contact boundaries at nonworking edges: two guide/stop strips through existing slots, two pivoting top keepers with remaining bolts, cork cushioning and accessible nonworking gloved grasp areas. Footprint and strip forming capacity must permit it.
openings.discriminator: Versus magnets assisted by cork friction, the cradle predicts similar displacement for both plates despite 7 N versus 3 N magnetic release checks; the rival may lose retention on the spare. Either prediction may fail: stroke loads, friction and cradle stiffness are unknown.
openings.probe: Use ruler and plate first to check slots, boundaries, keeper sweep and gloved grasp entirely outside marked stroke clearance, with the marked 30 mm edge exposed. Check M4 bolts fit slots and strips can be formed with supplied pliers. If feasible, drill only strips and fabricate within eighty minutes. Keep carriage attached to rails; do not drill, cut, heat or glue plate/carriage. Test one configuration: one original and two spare twenty-stroke runs, marking initial position and measuring displacement after five/twenty strokes. Perform one original and two gloved spare removal/return checks, timing service and verifying restored position and edge avoidance. Final run uses spare; removal uses thick gloves. Three runs and three service checks must fit twenty observation minutes if achievable. Magnetic configuration remains an untested rival prediction.
openings.uncertainty: Slot dimensions and strip thickness/formability/stiffness are unprovided. Unavailable capacity defeats design. Keeper/grasp clearance failure requires rejection without plate/carriage modification. Any displacement over 1 mm, service over sixty seconds, working-edge contact or interference defeats configuration. Three runs do not establish broader reliability.

lineage.reason: Mechanical relation, rival prediction, feasibility gates, uncertainty, declared uncertain fit, resource limits and defeat conditions retained.

decision: Check feasibility before fabrication; reject if capacity or clearance fails. Proceed only within supplied resources and hard constraints. This bounded fixture probe does not authorize deployment.
